exemplars.user: Build one part of the feature end to end, from the interface through the backend to the database, so I can test a real thing.
exemplars.output: Start with a vertical slice of the feature.

exemplars.user: The cards reorder and I want them to glide to their new positions so nothing jumps.
exemplars.output: Animate the card reorder with a FLIP animation.

exemplars.user: Make the thumbnail enlarge into the full-screen image on the next screen, it should feel like the same image carries over.
exemplars.output: Expand the thumbnail with a shared-element transition.

exemplars.user: The button sends the same request on every click and I need to avoid duplicate data.
exemplars.output: Make the button request idempotent.

exemplars.user: When the database updates, remove the stale cache so the next read is fresh.
exemplars.output: Invalidate the cache on every database write.

exemplars.user: Please fix the spelling of this word and remove the extra spaces, thanks.

exemplars.user: Fill the new required column for all existing rows without locking the database.
exemplars.output: Backfill the new column on existing rows in batches.

exemplars.user: Producers send work faster than workers can clear it, so they should slow down when the queue is full.
exemplars.output: Apply backpressure to the job queue when it fills up.

exemplars.user: The search fires a request on every keystroke and lags, it should wait until I stop typing.
exemplars.output: Debounce the search input by 300 milliseconds.

exemplars.user: Record each balance change as an event over time instead of only the final value, so we can audit full history.
exemplars.output: Model the user balance with event sourcing.

exemplars.user: The server already output the HTML, now bind the JavaScript and state to those nodes without re-rendering everything.
exemplars.output: Hydrate the server-rendered HTML with the interactive state.

exemplars.user: On login return a short-lived token for APIs and a long-lived one to renew when it expires.
exemplars.output: Use a short-lived access token with a refresh token.

exemplars.user: Searches on the users table are slow, so create an index that the query planner will use for this where clause.
exemplars.output: Add a database index matching the where clause.

exemplars.user: On signup, send the welcome email without making the user wait for it to finish before seeing the dashboard.
exemplars.output: Fire the welcome email asynchronously without blocking signup.

exemplars.user: Turn the new checkout on for a small percent of users first, and for everyone only when it is stable.

exemplars.user: Components that read part of the shared store should re-render automatically when that state changes.

exemplars.user: Move the whole login API to the new service gradually, keeping both versions running so no client breaks.
exemplars.output: Migrate the login API with a strangler-fig, so both versions are served.

exemplars.user: When the API keeps failing I don't want the app to keep hammering it and blow things up. Give it a pause after it fails a few times.
exemplars.output: Add a circuit breaker around the API calls so they stop after repeated failures.

exemplars.user: Emails that keep failing to send should be parked somewhere we can inspect later.
exemplars.output: Route the stuck emails to a dead-letter queue.

exemplars.user: Get the messages in pages by passing the last one we got so it keeps going from there.

exemplars.user: If any of these three inserts fail they should all roll back together.
exemplars.output: Wrap the three inserts in a transaction.

exemplars.user: As soon as the user clicks like, update the UI straight away and fix it if the server call fails.
